robot.name: Spirit AI Moz1
robot.status_notes: RoboBoom directory lists availability as Pilot. Gasgoo reports Moz robots have been introduced into JD.com retail settings for customer interaction and product demonstration. No official product page, price confirmation, or public sale channel was found.
intended_use_cases: office, meeting room cleaning and supply sorting
retail customer interaction and product demonstration
long-horizon room tidying from natural-language instructions
tea delivery and assistant scenarios (video titles only)

height.notes: RoboBoom directory spec; not independently confirmed by the company or a primary source.

weight.notes: RoboBoom directory spec; not independently confirmed by the company or a primary source.

payload.notes: Reported by RoboBoom, added 2026-10-29 by automated spec fill; Listed under Motion as 'Strength', not explicitly 'payload'; the same page also states a payload-to-weight ratio of 1:1 with 70 kg weight, so this figure is ambiguous..

runtime.notes: RoboBoom directory spec. A later video title claims a 4-hour stress test, but the content was not transcribed.

battery.notes: Battery capacity was not published in the reviewed sources.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: 26 DoF excluding the dexterous hand. Gasgoo reports 26 DoF; RoboBoom also lists 26 DoF excluding dex hand.

walking_speed.notes: RoboBoom lists walking speed 3.5 km/h and max speed 3.6 km/h. Moz1 uses a wheeled omnidirectional base, so 'walking speed' is a directory term for platform movement.

hands.description: Dual 7-DoF force/torque-position-hybrid bionic arms with 5 fingers per hand, according to RoboBoom. Full-body force control is claimed.
hands.force_feedback: full-body force control system (company claim via Gasgoo and RoboBoom)

items: whole-body STO safety with high-precision collision detection

compute.description: Industrial CPU + AI accelerator/GPU (assumed) according to RoboBoom. Runs Spirit AI's self-developed VLA model Spirit V1 / V1.6. Operating system Linux-based/ROS.

actuators.description: Electric servo motors with harmonic/compact precision gears. Gasgoo reports high power-density force-control joints and high-speed whole-body control algorithms.

availability.notes: RoboBoom directory lists price $150,000 and availability Pilot. No official company price or purchase path was found in the reviewed sources.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: RoboBoom and GlobalGPT describe Moz1 folding clothes, tidying offices, grabbing tissues, and executing dishwashing-related tasks such as loading dirty bowls. The WAIC 2026 demo reportedly put a cola in the refrigerator and loaded dirty bowls into the dishwasher. A video title claims office tea delivery using null space control.
caveats: No third-party dexterity benchmark or published success rates for Moz1 were found.
GlobalGPT's ~80% laundry success claim is a media summary, not a company-published metric.
Video content was not transcribed; titles only.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: RoboBoom timeline describes Moz1 executing a single natural-language instruction to tidy a living room at WAIC 2026, autonomously decomposing and replanning. A later training log is described as single-take with zero teleoperation under Spirit v1.6. Spirit v1.6 also topped the RoboArena benchmark at 1,924, but that is a model score, not robot execution.
caveats: Autonomy is company-asserted or summarized by RoboBoom; no intervention logs or independent audit were found.
The RoboArena benchmark evaluates the model, not the whole robot in a real environment.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Moz1 uses a high-dynamic omnidirectional wheeled base with dual 7-DoF arms and whole-body force control. RoboBoom lists max speed 3.6 km/h and walking speed 3.5 km/h.
caveats: Wheeled base, not a legged humanoid.
No independent mobility test, fall rate, or disturbance-recovery metric was found.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Spirit V1/V1.6 VLA model powers Moz1 with RGB+depth cameras and full-body force sensing. RoboBoom describes the robot re-perceiving the scene and replanning after disturbances during a tidy-up demo. The Spirit v1.6 model scored 1,924 on RoboArena.
caveats: No third-party perception benchmark for the integrated robot.
RoboArena is a model benchmark, not an onboard perception test.

human_interaction.summary: Gasgoo reports Moz robots have been introduced into JD.com retail settings for customer interaction and product demonstration. RoboBoom lists voice command support. A video title shows an assistant scenario.
caveats: No conversational reliability or interaction success metric was found.
JD.com deployment details are limited to a media summary.

endurance_reliability.summary: RoboBoom lists runtime 3 h. A 2026 video title claims a 4-hour stress test, but the video was not transcribed, so no results can be credited.
caveats: No failure rates, uptime logs, or independent endurance test data were found.
The stress test video title is not sufficient to verify performance.

human_environment_fit.summary: Moz1 is 160 cm tall and 70 kg according to RoboBoom, with a wheeled base and whole-body STO safety plus collision detection. Directory lists 'Safe with humans' as yes.
caveats: No third-party safety certification was found.
Directory safety rating is not verified.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Gasgoo reports Spirit AI's Moz robots have been introduced into JD.com retail settings. RoboBoom timeline also records a JD.com partnership announced 2026-03-19 to deploy Moz robots in JD MALL retail.
caveats: No unit count, hours, or performance metrics for the JD.com deployment were published.
The CATL Zhongzhou battery line deployment is attributed to a robot called Xiaomo, not Moz1, by Gasgoo and must not be credited to Moz1.

accessibility_value.summary: RoboBoom lists a price of $150,000 and availability Pilot, but no official purchase path or company-confirmed price was found.
caveats: Directory price is unverified and may not reflect actual commercial terms.

evidence_items.title: Gasgoo reports Spirit AI funding and Moz1 core specs
evidence_items.claim: Gasgoo reports Spirit AI raised nearly 2 billion yuan and that its in-house VLA model underpins Moz1, a full-body force-controlled humanoid robot with 26 degrees of freedom and a claimed 1:1 payload-to-weight ratio.
evidence_items.notes: Company claims reported by trade media.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Establishes the robot's core force-control architecture and funding for deployment.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Its in-house VLA model underpins the development of Moz1, a full-body force-controlled humanoid robot with 26 degrees of freedom.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Not an official spec page; relative improvements and payload ratio are company claims.

evidence_items.title: JD.com retail deployment for Moz robots
evidence_items.claim: Gasgoo reports Spirit AI's Moz robots have been introduced into JD.com retail settings for customer interaction and product demonstration tasks.
evidence_items.notes: The CATL battery line deployment in the same article is attributed to a robot called Xiaomo, not Moz1.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Provides named-customer deployment evidence for Moz robots, but without performance data.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Elsewhere, Spirit AI's Moz robots have been introduced into JD.com retail settings, taking on customer interaction and product demonstration tasks.
evidence_items.verification_notes: No unit count, hours, or autonomy details for the JD.com deployment were published.

evidence_items.title: RoboBoom key architectural specs
evidence_items.claim: RoboBoom lists Moz1 as having 26 DoF excluding dex hand, dual 7-DoF force/torque-position-hybrid bionic arms, a high-dynamic omnidirectional wheeled base, whole-body STO safety with collision detection, and a payload-to-weight ratio of 1:1.
evidence_items.notes: Directory spec; not independently verified by the company or a primary source.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Defines the wheeled humanoid architecture and safety features.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Key specs: 26 DoF (excluding dex hand) on a high-dynamic omnidirectional wheeled base; dual 7-DoF force / torque-position-hybrid bionic arms for anthropomorphic fine-grained operations; whole-body STO safety + high-precision collision detection; payload-to-weight ratio of 1:1.
evidence_items.verification_notes: RoboBoom is a directory; values should be treated cautiously.

evidence_items.title: GlobalGPT article on Moz1 capabilities
evidence_items.claim: GlobalGPT reports Moz1 has 26 degrees of freedom, a 15% power density lead over Tesla Optimus, and can fold laundry with about 80% success rates.
evidence_items.notes: Article refers to the company as Qianxun Intelligence, possibly the same as Spirit AI. Claims are not independently verified.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Provides early third-party media summary of dexterity and autonomy.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: For instance, folding laundry—a seemingly simple but actually complex task due to fabric variability—becomes possible with ~80% success rates.
evidence_items.source_location: GlobalGPT article, Under the Hood section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Not a primary source; success rate source not cited beyond article.

evidence_items.title: WAIC 2026 single-instruction room tidying demo
evidence_items.claim: At WAIC 2026, Spirit AI demonstrated Moz1 running Spirit v1.6 performing a single natural-language instruction to tidy a living/dining area, autonomously decomposing and replanning, including putting a cola in the refrigerator and loading dirty bowls into the dishwasher.
evidence_items.notes: Timeline summary from RoboBoom, not a primary video source.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Demonstrates long-horizon task execution from natural language.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: At the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, Spirit AI demonstrated Moz1 running the upgraded Spirit v1.6 embodied model.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Secondary summary; video content not transcribed. Autonomy described as autonomous but no intervention log.

evidence_items.title: Single-take training log with zero teleoperation
evidence_items.claim: Spirit AI released a single-take training log in which Moz1 is given one instruction to tidy up a living room and executes the whole long-horizon task autonomously under Spirit v1.6, including three rounds of unexpected disturbances, with the company stating zero teleoperation.
evidence_items.notes: RoboBoom summary of company video. Zero teleoperation is a company claim.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Strongest autonomy claim for Moz1, but not independently verified.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Spirit AI released a single-take training log in which Moz1 is given one instruction - 'Tidy up the living room' - and executes the whole long-horizon task autonomously under Spirit v1.6.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company-asserted autonomy; no external audit. Disturbance details from RoboBoom summary.

evidence_items.title: Spirit v1.6 tops RoboArena benchmark
evidence_items.claim: Spirit AI's foundation model Spirit v1.6, which powers Moz1, scored 1,924 on the RoboArena benchmark, surpassing Nvidia's Cosmos3-Nano-Policy at 1,881 to become the first Chinese model to top the leaderboard.
evidence_items.notes: Benchmark result for the model, not the integrated robot.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Provides some external benchmark evidence for the underlying VLA model.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Spirit AI's foundation model for embodied intelligence, Spirit v1.6 (powering Moz1), scored 1,924 on the RoboArena benchmark, surpassing Nvidia's Cosmos3-Nano-Policy at 1,881 to become the first Chinese model to top the leaderboard.
evidence_items.verification_notes: RoboArena is a benchmark, but this is a model score, not whole-robot validation.

evidence_items.title: Missing disclosures
evidence_items.claim: No battery capacity, hand DoF, official price, purchase path, intervention logs, or independent verification were found for Spirit AI Moz1. Video titles provide only limited claims without transcripts.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Judges should reduce confidence on endurance, accessibility, and autonomy.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Gaps identified across all reviewed primary and secondary sources.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Absence of disclosure, not evidence of inability.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Spirit AI Moz1 is a wheeled humanoid with force-controlled arms and a VLA model. Public evidence shows promising long-horizon room tidying demos and JD.com retail deployment mentions, but most claims are company-asserted or directory-sourced, and official specs, price, endurance data, and independent verification are missing.
strongest_positive_evidence: RoboBoom timeline describes a single-take, zero-teleoperation long-horizon tidy-up with disturbance replanning under Spirit v1.6.
Gasgoo reports JD.com retail deployment for Moz robots with customer interaction and product demonstration.
RoboBoom records Spirit v1.6 topping RoboArena benchmark at 1,924.
Multiple official video titles suggest real-world assistant, tea delivery, and stress-test scenarios.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No official product page, official price, battery capacity, hand DoF, or purchase path.
No independent endurance or autonomy benchmark for the integrated robot.
Video content for all titles is not transcribed; no capability can be verified from them.
No performance metrics for JD.com deployment.
conflicting_claims: Company naming: Gasgoo and RoboBoom use 'Spirit AI', while GlobalGPT uses 'Qianxun Intelligence'.

CATL deployment: Gasgoo attributes the CATL Zhongzhou battery line deployment to a robot called 'Xiaomo', not Moz1, while RoboBoom's funding item says 'Moz1 force-controlled humanoid already on CATL battery production lines.'
Payload: Gasgoo claims 1:1 payload-to-weight ratio, but RoboBoom lists 'Strength 26 kg' without clear payload definition.
Price: RoboBoom lists $150,000, but no official Spirit AI price or store was found.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit CATL Zhongzhou zero-defect battery production to Moz1; that is Xiaomo per Gasgoo.
Do not treat RoboBoom directory specs (height, weight, runtime, price) as official.
Do not treat video titles as evidence of autonomy or endurance without transcript review.
Do not describe Moz1 as bipedal; it is a wheeled humanoid.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Spirit AI Moz1 is a Chinese wheeled humanoid with 26 DoF, dual 7-DoF force-controlled arms, and an omnidirectional base, running the Spirit VLA model. Evidence includes RoboBoom directory specs (160 cm, 70 kg, 3 h runtime, $150,000 price) and company-related demos of long-horizon room tidying from a single instruction, including a single-take video claimed to have zero teleoperation. Gasgoo reports Moz robots in JD.com retail settings for customer interaction. No official product page, official price, battery capacity, or independent endurance/autonomy verification was found; video titles for several demos are not transcribed. The CATL battery line deployment is attributed to Xiaomo, not Moz1, and must not be credited here.
strongest_evidence: RoboBoom timeline describes a single-take, zero-teleoperation long-horizon tidy-up with disturbances under Spirit v1.6.
Gasgoo reports JD.com retail deployment for Moz robots.
RoboBoom records Spirit v1.6 topping RoboArena benchmark.
Official video titles suggest real-world scenarios such as tea delivery and stress testing.
weakest_evidence: No official specs, price, or purchase path.
No independent endurance or autonomy benchmark for the integrated robot.
Video titles only; no transcripts to verify capabilities.
known_do_not_credit: CATL Zhongzhou battery line deployment (Xiaomo, not Moz1).
Official price or availability beyond pilot status.
Endurance or autonomy claims from video titles only.
